title: Optimization of multi-objective flexible scheduling for container rail mounted gantry cranes in railway logistics yards.
problem: The efficiency of rail-mounted gantry crane (RMG) operations directly affects train handling performance in railway logistics terminals.
contribution: This study develops a revised multi-objective scheduling framework for flexible RMG operations in railway container terminals.
method: The framework combines resource enumeration, initial crane layout optimization, and an improved genetic algorithm with adaptive operators and tabu-search-based local refinement.
data_setup: Xi'an International Port Station with 110 container tasks and five RMGs.
results: The proposed IGA obtained an average completion time of 752.4 min under the baseline configuration and remained feasible under tested safety-distance and crane-number scenarios.
limitations: The claims are limited to the reported instance, and the method is presented as a reproducible heuristic rather than a proof of global optimality.
